minorMood: Natural minor usually feels stable and emotional.
Phrygian adds more tension through the flat second.
Minor pentatonic keeps melodies focused and uncluttered.
melodyRules: Wide leaps feel more dramatic when they resolve by step.
A short repeated motif gets stronger when one note changes at the bar turn.
Leaving rests between phrases helps a sparse melody feel intentional.
counterMelody: A counter line should usually fill rhythmic gaps instead of mirroring every hit.
Use a different register and simpler rhythm than the lead if the main motif is already active.
Support notes around chord tones first, then add passing tones for motion.
